correctness.rationale: The exact derivative identity was reconstructed from the stated vector field and checked symbolically. For \(a\le d\), \(d>0\), \(c>0\), its defect is nonnegative with zero set \(x=y=0\). Bounded-orbit monotonicity plus uniform continuity yields \(x,y,z\to0\); the two-sided version makes every bounded complete orbit constant. Strict monotonicity of \(\sinh x/x\) proves the sharp converse for \(a>d\). The theorem explicitly does not claim global boundedness.

value.rationale: The parameter surface \(a=d\) is the source-defined pitchfork boundary, not an arbitrary slice. Proving it is also the exact global threshold for existence of any nontrivial compact invariant set closes the full nonhyperbolic side \(a\le d\), including the boundary, and rigorously excludes periodic or chaotic compact recurrence there without a local-stability assumption. The invariant-measure formulation is a natural statistical consequence of the same structural law.
